newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower on foreign funds indecision.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower on foreign funds indecision.

text.p: Foreign institutional funds could not decide whether to aggressively buy Malaysian shares on Monday, contributing to a small fall on blue-chip stocks, analysts and dealers said.

"U.S. fund managers can delay their decision on whether to stay in the U.S. market or to invest aggressively in Asia, up to the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in December," said Razani Radzi, head of research at PB Securities.
The Composite Index of 100 leading Malaysian stocks dropped 1.68 points to close at 1148.50, after rising to 1152.43 at midday.
Second Board stocks continued to fall as local technical analysts advised punters to sell their holdings of small-capitalised stocks.
The Second Board Index fell 12.22 points to 558.97.
Volume continued to be high with 273 million shares traded, valued at 1,946 million ringgit. Losers led gainers 424 to 173, with 127 stocks unchanged.

TRI -- up 85 cents at 7.45 -- was the day's most actively-traded stock with nearly 26 million shares changing hands. Analysts said the activity was due to Deutsche Telekom buying TRI shares under a deal announced in June.
